text:
maria: Draft PRD: Observability Console — retention & UX flows. Link: https://docs.internal/redwood/prd/observability-retention-draft — please review. TL;DR: customer asks for workspace-level retention controls, want clear cost visibility, and rollout gates. Need scope decision: full per-route controls vs workspace presets? Also proposing launch gates and acceptance criteria.

alex: Quick skim, thanks. My vote: ship workspace presets first, delay per-route to a later iteration. Gives customers control while keeping surface small.

jonathan: +1. Per-route expands index/partitioning complexity and billing logic. For presets we should provide API + Console. Rough estimate: backend ~3 sprints, console ~1 sprint (depends on infra).

tara: From design POV: presets need a clear default, and an "advanced" toggle for power-users. I added two mock flows (edit modal + cost preview). Need microcopy for "retention window" and consequences of longer retention.

kevin: SRE note: retention changes affect object TTLs and possible reindex/backfill. Backfill can cause big egress/spike. Recommend: no automatic backfill for extended retention; offer an opt-in paid backfill job. Also need safe throttles for storage ops.

maria: Good catch @kevin — adding to ACs. Proposed acceptance criteria (draft): - AC1: Admins can set workspace retention from Console and API with options [7d, 30d, 90d, 365d]. - AC2: Console shows projected storage delta and estimated monthly cost before apply. - AC3: No automatic backfill; optional paid backfill job must be explicitly requested. - AC4: Rollout strategy supports canary -> staged increments (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and automated fallback to global default on failures. - AC5: Queries older than retention return a friendly message with link to docs and support.

alex: Launch criteria checklist: docs + migration guide, API/SDK tests, billing estimate + support runbook, Console UX in staging, telemetry thresholds defined (error-rate spike <1% and storage increase within projected bounds during canary). Sound right?

jonathan: A couple engineering questions: how do we compute the "projected storage delta" efficiently? Running live histograms per change is heavy. I suggest we rely on precomputed monthly ingest metrics per workspace and apply a multiplier based on selected retention window. Also need a clear rollback plan for partial failures (e.g., TTL changes applied to some buckets).

tara: UX edge cases: 1) workspaces with custom compressed traces — tooltip explaining estimate variance; 2) users with many projects — add bulk edit for workspace presets (backlog); 3) if a workspace has active long-running queries, changing retention should surface warnings.

maria: Decision (proposed scope for launch): Console + API support for workspace-level presets, cost-estimate modal, no per-route retention, opt-in paid backfill only, staged feature-flag rollout. Action items: - jonathan: provide detailed effort estimate + infra checklist by Wed - kevin: draft rollback & backfill policy + throttling guidelines by Wed - tara: final mocks and microcopy by Thu - alex: finalize launch gates, telemetry thresholds, and support playbook by Fri

jonathan: Will do. Initial estimate here: backend 6w, infra 2w, console 2w (parallelizable) — roughly 3 sprints total. I'll add endpoints and infra checklist to the PRD.

deploy-bot: prod-deploy:note: Recommendation: automate staged rollout with feature flags. Proposed tag: observability.retention.workspace.v1 — supports % rollouts and easy rollback.

alex: :thumbsup: Good momentum. Can we do a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00am to confirm mocks and launch gates?

maria: Yes, added to calendar. Thanks everyone.
